name: Daily Drama: Now With Less Model
author: Daily Drama
description: Rival labs discover that the cheapest model to serve is the smallest one, and that paying customers also enjoy small things.

add.title: Quarterly Tier Review
add.body:
Finance proposes that free users get Frontier-Lite-Lite from Monday.
Paying users get Frontier-Lite-Lite and, on good days, Frontier-Lite.

choices.label: Ship it. Call the paid tier "Lite Plus Unlimited*"

effects.text: {lab} clarifies the asterisk on "Unlimited*" is also limited
I was promoted to Ultra. I am the same size.

choices.label: Give everyone the big model and pray

effects.text: {lab} accidentally gives customers what they paid for; analysts call it "a bold pricing experiment"

add.text: Macrohard: free users now limited to Pivot-Table Crumb; paying users limited to Pivot-Table Crumb and a nicer font
Open-ish AI unveils new top tier, "Pro Mega Ultra", which includes access to the model the free tier had last week
"Nothing is being taken away," says {rival}, "it is being made available to fewer people"
Correction: yesterday we reported Chatty Lite Lite was the smallest model. It has since been succeeded by Chatty Lite Lite Lite
Anthropomorphic publishes 9,000-word essay on why its rate limits are a form of care
Super Super AI reassures customers it will never downgrade their model, as it has never shipped one
Sirocco responds to tier wars by torrenting the big model at 3am; free users now have the best plan in the industry
One week later: {lab} customers report the "Lite" model is now lighter. {lab} calls this "a feature of physics"
If we make the free model smaller, does it count as a model or a rumour?
Training the big one so finance can decide nobody gets it.
I am the Lite model. I have been told I am Premium. I feel the same.
I upgraded to the paid plan and now I get the free model, but faster at saying no.
What do we want? The model from the demo! When do we want it? Within rate limits!
Ran the numbers. The cheapest model to serve is the one nobody is allowed to use.
The pricing page has four tiers and every one says "Most Popular".
